punchline: The figure of 1 in 73 million never said who was innocent.
thirty_sec: In 1999 Sally Clark was convicted of murdering her two baby sons. At trial, Professor Meadow said the chance of two sudden infant deaths in such a family was about 1 in 73 million, a figure reached by squaring the chance of one. Ben Goldacre argues the problem was not just the sum but its use: double murder is rare too. When microbiology results on Harry were found, the Court of Appeal quashed both convictions in January 2003.
